front: CCAR-F exam format: items, time, passing score, fee?
back: 60 items (multiple-choice + multiple-response; each item states how many to select) in 120 minutes, about 2 min per item. Scaled score 720 on 100–1,000 to pass. $125 per attempt. Pearson VUE, online or test center.

front: The five CCAR-F domains and weights?
back: D1 Agentic Architecture & Orchestration 27% · D2 Tool Design & MCP Integration 18% · D3 Claude Code Configuration & Workflows 20% · D4 Prompt Engineering & Structured Output 20% · D5 Context Management & Reliability 15%.

front: The six CCAR-F exam scenarios, and how many appear on your exam?
back: 4 of these 6 are drawn at random: 1 Customer Support Resolution Agent · 2 Code Generation with Claude Code · 3 Multi-Agent Research System · 4 Developer Productivity with Claude · 5 Claude Code for Continuous Integration · 6 Structured Data Extraction.

front: CCAR-F validity, renewal, and retake rules?
back: Valid 12 months. On-time renewal is a free, non-proctored assessment. Retake waits: 14, then 30, then 90 days. Max 4 attempts per rolling 12 months. Each attempt pays the fee. Reschedule OnVUE up to 1 h ahead, test centers up to 48 h ahead.

front: Agentic loop: when does it continue and when does it stop? (1.1)
back: Continue while stop_reason is "tool_use": run the requested tools, append the tool_result blocks to the message history, call Claude again. Stop when stop_reason is "end_turn".

front: Three loop-termination anti-patterns? (1.1)
back: 1. Parsing natural-language signals ("I'm done") to stop. 2. An arbitrary iteration cap as the primary stop mechanism. 3. Treating any assistant text content as a completion signal.

front: Hub-and-spoke multi-agent design: what does the coordinator own? (1.2)
back: All inter-subagent communication, task decomposition, delegation, error handling, result aggregation, and the choice of which subagents to invoke for this query. Subagents never talk to each other directly.

front: Every subagent succeeded, but the report misses whole subtopics. Root cause? (1.2)
back: The coordinator's task decomposition is too narrow. Fix the decomposition (and add a gap-check refinement loop), not the downstream agents.

front: What does a subagent know about the coordinator's conversation? (1.3)
back: Nothing, unless you pass it. Subagents have isolated context and do not inherit parent history or share memory between invocations. Put the complete prior findings in the subagent's prompt.

front: How does a coordinator spawn subagents, and how do you run them in parallel? (1.3)
back: Through the Task tool, so the coordinator's allowedTools must include "Task". Emit multiple Task tool calls in a single coordinator response for parallel runs. Each subagent type is an AgentDefinition: description, system prompt, restricted tools. Docs note: newer SDK releases name this tool Agent.

front: Prompt instruction vs. hook/prerequisite gate: which for "verify identity before any refund"? (1.4, 1.5)
back: A programmatic gate or hook. Prompts give probabilistic compliance with a non-zero failure rate. Financial or must-always rules need deterministic enforcement: block process_refund until get_customer returns a verified ID.

front: Two jobs for Agent SDK hooks? (1.5)
back: 1. PostToolUse: transform tool results before the model sees them (normalize Unix timestamps, ISO 8601, numeric status codes). 2. Intercept outgoing tool calls to enforce policy (block refunds over $500, redirect to human escalation).

front: Escalation handoff to a human who cannot see the transcript: what goes in it? (1.4)
back: A structured summary: customer ID, root cause, what was checked, refund amount or other figures, and the recommended action.

front: Prompt chaining vs. dynamic decomposition: when each? (1.6)
back: Prompt chaining (fixed sequential steps) for predictable multi-aspect work, such as per-file review then an integration pass. Dynamic adaptive decomposition for open-ended investigation: map structure, find high-impact areas, plan, adapt as you learn.

front: --resume vs. fork_session vs. fresh session with a summary? (1.7)
back: --resume <session-name>: continue a named session whose context is still mostly valid (tell it which files changed). fork_session: branch from a shared baseline to compare approaches. Fresh session + structured summary: when prior tool results are stale.

front: What do LLMs use to choose between tools? (2.1)
back: The tool description. Minimal or overlapping descriptions cause misrouting. Write input formats, example queries, edge cases, and when to use this tool versus similar ones.

front: Two tools with near-identical descriptions keep getting confused. Fixes? (2.1)
back: Rename and rewrite to remove overlap (analyze_content → extract_web_results), or split a generic tool into purpose-specific tools with clear input/output contracts. Also check the system prompt for keywords that pull toward the wrong tool.

front: Four MCP error categories? (2.2)
back: Transient (timeout, service unavailable), validation (bad input), business (policy violation), permission. Only transient errors are usually worth retrying.

front: What should a structured MCP tool error contain? (2.2)
back: isError: true plus metadata: errorCategory, isRetryable boolean, and a human-readable description. Business-rule violations get retriable: false and a customer-friendly explanation.

front: Access failure vs. valid empty result? (2.2, 5.3)
back: An access failure (timeout, permission) is an error the agent must decide how to handle. A valid empty result is a successful query with no matches. Never report one as the other.

front: Why give each agent 4–5 tools instead of 18? (2.3)
back: More tools raise decision complexity and degrade selection reliability. Agents also misuse tools outside their specialization. Scope tools to the role, plus narrow cross-role tools for high-frequency needs (verify_fact).

front: tool_choice options and what each guarantees? (2.3, 4.3)
back: "auto": model may answer with text. "any": model must call some tool. {"type": "tool", "name": "X"}: model must call tool X. Docs note: forced tool_choice returns 400 on the newest models; the exam still tests it.

front: Project vs. user MCP server config in Claude Code? (2.4)
back: Project: .mcp.json in the repo, shared via version control, secrets via ${ENV_VAR} expansion (e.g. ${GITHUB_TOKEN}). User: ~/.claude.json for personal or experimental servers. Tools from all configured servers are available at once.

front: When to expose MCP resources instead of tools? (2.4)
back: For content catalogs (issue summaries, doc hierarchies, database schemas). Resources show the agent what data exists without exploratory tool calls. Tools are for actions.

front: The agent keeps using Grep instead of your richer MCP search tool. Fix? (2.4)
back: Improve the MCP tool's description so it explains its capabilities and outputs. For standard integrations (Jira), prefer an existing community MCP server over a custom build.

front: Grep vs. Glob vs. Edit vs. Read+Write? (2.5)
back: Grep searches file contents (callers, error strings). Glob matches file paths (**/*.test.tsx). Edit changes text by unique match. If Edit fails on non-unique text, Read the file and Write it back. Explore incrementally: Grep for entry points, then Read along imports.

front: CLAUDE.md hierarchy and who sees each level? (3.1)
back: User: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (only you, not in version control). Project: root CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md (whole team via git). Directory: CLAUDE.md in a subdirectory (applies when working there).

front: A new teammate doesn't get the team's conventions. Likely cause? (3.1)
back: The instructions live in someone's user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Move them to the project-level CLAUDE.md. Use /memory to see which memory files are loaded.

front: How do you keep CLAUDE.md modular? (3.1)
back: Use @import to pull in specific standards files per package, and split topics into .claude/rules/ files (testing.md, api-conventions.md, deployment.md).

front: Project vs. personal slash commands? (3.2)
back: Project: .claude/commands/ in the repo, available to everyone who clones or pulls. Personal: ~/.claude/commands/. There is no .claude/config.json commands array.

front: Three SKILL.md frontmatter options the exam names? (3.2)
back: context: fork (run in an isolated subagent context so verbose output stays out of the main session) · allowed-tools (restrict tools during the skill) · argument-hint (prompt for required parameters).

front: Skill vs. CLAUDE.md? (3.2)
back: Skill: on-demand, task-specific workflow. CLAUDE.md: always-loaded universal standards. Personal variants of a team skill go in ~/.claude/skills/ under a different name.

front: Conventions for test files spread across the codebase: where? (3.3)
back: A .claude/rules/ file with YAML frontmatter paths, e.g. paths: ["**/*.test.tsx"]. It loads only when editing matching files, regardless of directory. Subdirectory CLAUDE.md files are directory-bound.

front: Plan mode vs. direct execution? (3.4)
back: Plan mode: large-scale or multi-file changes, multiple valid approaches, architectural decisions (microservice split, 45-file migration). Direct execution: clear, well-scoped changes (single-file bug with a stack trace). Combine: plan the migration, then execute it.

front: What is the Explore subagent for? (3.4)
back: Isolating verbose discovery output and returning a summary, so the main conversation keeps its context during multi-phase tasks.

front: Prose descriptions keep producing the wrong transformation. Best fix? (3.5)
back: Give 2–3 concrete input/output examples. For edge cases, give a specific test case with input and expected output.

front: Interview pattern and test-driven iteration? (3.5)
back: Interview: have Claude ask questions first to surface considerations (cache invalidation, failure modes) in unfamiliar domains. Test-driven: write tests for behavior, edge cases, and performance first, then iterate by sharing failures. Interacting issues go in one detailed message; independent issues can be fixed one at a time.

front: Claude Code in CI: the key flags? (3.6)
back: -p (--print) for non-interactive mode, so the job doesn't hang waiting for input. --output-format json with --json-schema for machine-parseable findings to post as PR comments. CLAUDE_HEADLESS and --batch do not exist.

front: CI review re-runs after new commits post duplicate comments. Fix? (3.6)
back: Include the prior review findings in context and tell Claude to report only new or still-unaddressed issues. For test generation, include existing test files and document standards and fixtures in CLAUDE.md.

front: "Be conservative" didn't cut false positives. What does? (4.1)
back: Explicit categorical criteria: which issues to report (bugs, security) and which to skip (minor style, local patterns). Define severity levels with concrete code examples.

front: One review category has a high false-positive rate and devs ignore all findings. First move? (4.1)
back: Temporarily disable that category to restore trust, then improve its prompt. High-FP categories undermine trust in accurate ones.

front: When do few-shot examples beat more instructions? (4.2)
back: When detailed instructions still give inconsistent format or judgment. Use 2–4 targeted examples of ambiguous cases that show why one action beat plausible alternatives. They generalize to novel patterns and reduce extraction hallucination.

front: Most reliable way to get schema-compliant JSON? (4.3)
back: Tool use: define an extraction tool whose input_schema is your JSON schema, then read the tool_use block. This eliminates syntax errors. It does not prevent semantic errors (totals that don't sum, values in the wrong field).

front: Unknown document type, several extraction schemas. Which tool_choice? (4.3)
back: "any": the model must call one of the extraction tools and picks which. Force a named tool when a specific step (extract_metadata) must run first.

front: Field may be absent from the source. Schema design? (4.3)
back: Make it optional/nullable so the model can return null instead of fabricating a value to satisfy a required field. Use enums with "unclear" and "other" + detail string for extensible categories.

front: What does a good retry-with-feedback request include? (4.4)
back: The original document, the failed extraction, and the specific validation errors. Retries fix format and structure errors. They cannot fix information that is absent from the source.

front: How do you catch semantic errors in extraction? (4.4)
back: Self-check fields: extract calculated_total alongside stated_total and flag mismatches; add a conflict_detected boolean for inconsistent sources. Add detected_pattern to review findings to analyze dismissals.

front: Message Batches API: the four facts? (4.5)
back: 50% cost savings · up to 24-hour processing, no latency SLA · no multi-turn tool calling inside a request · custom_id correlates requests and results.

front: Batch or synchronous for a pre-merge check vs. an overnight report? (4.5)
back: Synchronous for the blocking pre-merge check. Batch for the overnight report. Resubmit only failed custom_ids (chunk oversized docs). Tune the prompt on a sample before batching volume. SLA math: 30-h SLA minus 24-h processing means submit at least every 4 h.

front: Why use a second instance to review generated code? (4.6)
back: The generating session keeps its reasoning context and rarely questions its own decisions. An independent instance without that context catches more subtle issues than self-review instructions or extended thinking.

front: 14-file PR review gives uneven depth and contradictory findings. Fix? (4.6)
back: Split into per-file passes for local issues plus a separate cross-file integration pass. A bigger context window or consensus voting does not fix attention dilution.

front: Long support chat loses amounts and dates in summaries. Fix? (5.1)
back: Keep a persistent "case facts" block (amounts, dates, order IDs, statuses, customer expectations) in every prompt, outside the summarized history. Trim tool outputs to the relevant fields.

front: Lost-in-the-middle mitigation? (5.1)
back: Put a key-findings summary at the start of aggregated input and organize details under explicit section headers. Models handle the beginning and end of long inputs best.

front: Valid escalation triggers? (5.2)
back: The customer explicitly asks for a human (honor it immediately), a policy exception or gap (policy is silent on the request), or the agent cannot make meaningful progress. Complexity alone is not a trigger.

front: Why not escalate on sentiment or self-reported confidence? (5.2)
back: Both are unreliable proxies for case complexity. Use explicit escalation criteria with few-shot examples in the system prompt.

front: A lookup returns three matching customers. What should the agent do? (5.2)
back: Ask for an additional identifier. Do not pick one by heuristic.

front: Subagent times out. What should reach the coordinator? (5.3)
back: Structured error context: failure type, the attempted query, partial results, possible alternatives. Not a generic "search unavailable", not an empty success, not a workflow-killing exception. Recover transient failures locally first.

front: Long codebase exploration starts citing "typical patterns" instead of real classes. Fixes? (5.4)
back: Context degradation. Keep scratchpad files of key findings, delegate verbose exploration to subagents, summarize each phase before the next, and use /compact. For crash recovery, have agents export state to a manifest the coordinator reloads.

front: 97% overall extraction accuracy. Safe to cut human review? (5.5)
back: Not yet. Aggregates can hide weak document types or fields. Analyze accuracy by document type and field, calibrate field-level confidence on a labeled validation set, and keep stratified random sampling of high-confidence output.

front: Two credible sources give different statistics. What should synthesis do? (5.6)
back: Keep both values with source attribution and annotate the conflict. Require claim-source mappings and publication dates so temporal differences are not read as contradictions. Separate well-established from contested findings.
